bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Steel price volatility in the pipes business — The Board's Report states the steel pipes & strips segment delivered its operational performance 'despite continued steel prices volatility'. As a converter of steel into ERW, GI, API, spiral and coated pipes, input-price swings feed directly into realisations and segment profitability, which fell year on year.
- Muted demand for high value-added pipe products — Management attributes the marginal fall in steel segment revenue and the drop in segment profitability mainly to a slowdown in demand for high value-added products, only marginally offset by better sales in all other pipe categories - the mix, not the volume, is what carries segment margin.
- Dependence on government-led project execution — The Board's Report flags 'slower execution across certain government led projects' as a condition the steel segment operated through during the year. Structural and galvanised pipe demand is tied to public project award and execution, so slippage transmits straight to segment volumes.
- Geopolitical disruption and export-market exposure — Performance was delivered 'in-spite of geopolitical disruptions' and amid 'geographical uncertainties'. Products are exported to more than 50 countries with a strong foothold in the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) nations, so regional disruption in export markets is a direct revenue risk.
- Trade-policy and safeguard-duty exposure — The Board's Report cites 'safe-guard duty implementation' among the conditions the steel pipes segment operated through during the year - trade-remedy and tariff changes alter both landed input cost and export competitiveness.
- Brand reputation and product-quality / customer-grievance risk — Identified in the BRSR material responsible business conduct issues table as a risk: as a well-established household brand with a large customer base, any adverse customer experience, product quality concern, service deficiency or delay in grievance resolution may cause customer attrition and weaken brand loyalty, with negative implications for long-term growth and market position.
- Business ethics, governance and compliance breaches — Flagged in the BRSR material issues table: any deviation from ethical, legal or governance standards may expose the Company to compliance risk, reputational concerns, stakeholder dissatisfaction and business disruption. Mitigated through a formal Code of Conduct covering Directors, employees, vendors and customers, a vigil mechanism overseen by the Audit Committee, and a Board-level Risk Management Committee that monitors risks and controls.
- Energy cost, emissions and climate-related regulatory exposure — The BRSR material issues table identifies energy management as both risk and opportunity: inefficient energy consumption may raise operating costs, contribute to higher greenhouse gas emissions and expose the Company to climate-related and regulatory risk across its manufacturing units, addressed through its Environment, Health and Safety Policy and replacement of high-energy-consuming lighting-manufacturing equipment.

outlook.body: Surya Roshni continued brownfield capacity building across its steel pipe network during 2025-26. The Board's report states that capacity expansion initiatives across Anjar, Gwalior, Bahadurgarh and Hindupur, along with the addition of new DFT (Direct Forming Technology) lines, are aligned to support the growth trajectory in structural, API and value-added pipes; the Chairman similarly reports that capacity expansions continued across Bahadurgarh, Gwalior, Anjar and Hindupur, aimed at strengthening participation in structural pipes, API pipes, spiral pipes and value-added applications. Ramp-up at newer facilities, particularly spiral and Cold Rolled Strips (CRS) operations, is described as progressing in line with internal benchmarks and supporting incremental operating leverage, with capacity utilisation across plants remaining well balanced and production redirected internally towards higher-demand, value-accretive categories. During the year the segment achieved a first-in-India milestone by manufacturing API 5CT casing pipes using ERW technology, which enabled an order from Oil and Natural Gas Corporation. On the consumer side, entry into wires and cables was backed by an investment of Rs 25 crore, with the Turbo Flex range manufactured entirely in-house at the Malanpur facility. The AR's history line-up records the preceding build-out: the Hindupur steel pipe plant (2017, scaled to 1,50,000 MT), 3LPE coated pipe units at Anjar (2019 and 2021), a third galvanised plant at Hindupur taking total capacity to 2,00,000 MT (2021), a large-diameter DFT facility at Gwalior (2022), LED component manufacturing including drivers, PCBs, MCPCBs, housings and diffusers (2023), spiral pipe production at Gwalior and a new cold rolled plant at Bahadurgarh (2024-25), and in 2025-26 advanced backward integration through LED component manufacturing under the PLI scheme.

- Large-scale Indian investments in infrastructure development, urbanisation, industrial growth, energy transition, water security and rising consumer aspirations are expected to drive demand across both business segments
- Government thrust on increasing the share of gas in the energy mix, City Gas Distribution networks, domestic water, irrigation projects and the 'Har Ghar Jal' scheme is expected to benefit the Company's existing GI pipe capacities and rural distribution presence
- Demand from infrastructure, industrial fabrication and engineering applications remains strong and is described as increasingly becoming the backbone of the medium-term growth strategy
- Global supply chains are undergoing structural change, with customers seeking diversified sourcing alternatives — an opportunity for Indian manufacturers, though Middle East geopolitical developments disrupted shipment schedules in the latter part of the year
- Ramp-up at newer facilities, particularly spiral and Cold Rolled Strips (CRS) operations, is progressing in line with internal benchmarks and supports incremental operating leverage
- Product-mix shift towards value-added products supports better margins, stronger customer relationships and greater export potential
- Professional Lighting demand is driven by large-scale investment in urban development, mobility upgradation, industrial facilities, commercial hubs and public infrastructure
- Headwinds flagged on the export front: quota restrictions in Europe and Canada, introduction of CBAM (Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism) in Europe, and widening price gaps between domestic and international steel prices
- API pipe volumes remained subdued, declining sharply year-on-year due to a slowdown in tender activity; steel price volatility, safeguard duty implementation and slower execution of certain government-led projects weighed on the year
- Manufacturing capability breadth — the Company states it is the only player in India able to manufacture MS pipes from 0.6 mm to 25 mm thickness and pipe sizes from half an inch to 140 inches, on a manufacturing capacity of 14.21 lakh tonnes per annum
- Registration in Neom city, a new urban area planned by Saudi Arabia, is expected to enable supply of pipes to new city projects, with active enquiries already received
- Steel business order book exceeding Rs 1,000 crore at year-end, led primarily by exports, spiral pipes and domestic API orders, providing strong visibility going into 2026-27
- Professional Lighting concluded the year with an order book of Rs 160 crore, providing healthy near-term visibility
- Order from Oil and Natural Gas Corporation secured after successfully manufacturing API 5CT casing pipes using ERW technology for the first time in India

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Surya Roshni is a diversified Indian manufacturer of steel pipes & strips and of lighting and consumer durables, describing itself as the largest exporter of ERW pipes and the largest producer of ERW GI pipes in India.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: The Company manufactures ERW steel pipes (GI, black, hollow section), API and welded pipes, spiral pipes, 3LPE coated pipes and CR strips & sheets, serving construction, scaffolding, casing, borewell tubing, agriculture, irrigation, firefighting, water transport, oil & gas and general industrial usage in domestic and export markets. Its second vertical spans lighting and consumer durables, covering LED and conventional lighting for consumer and professional applications, fans, home appliances and, since 2025-26, domestic house wires. Products are sold through an extensive dealer and retailer distribution network under the Surya brand, supported by in-house manufacturing and the Surya Technology & Innovation Centre.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Large-scale Indian investments in infrastructure development, urbanisation, industrial growth, energy transition, water security and rising consumer aspirations are expected to drive demand across both business segments
- Government thrust on increasing the share of gas in the energy mix, City Gas Distribution networks, domestic water, irrigation projects and the 'Har Ghar Jal' scheme is expected to benefit the Company's existing GI pipe capacities and rural distribution presence
- Demand from infrastructure, industrial fabrication and engineering applications remains strong and is described as increasingly becoming the backbone of the medium-term growth strategy
- Global supply chains are undergoing structural change, with customers seeking diversified sourcing alternatives — an opportunity for Indian manufacturers, though Middle East geopolitical developments disrupted shipment schedules in the latter part of the year
- Ramp-up at newer facilities, particularly spiral and Cold Rolled Strips (CRS) operations, is progressing in line with internal benchmarks and supports incremental operating leverage
- Product-mix shift towards value-added products supports better margins, stronger customer relationships and greater export potential
- Professional Lighting demand is driven by large-scale investment in urban development, mobility upgradation, industrial facilities, commercial hubs and public infrastructure
- Headwinds flagged on the export front: quota restrictions in Europe and Canada, introduction of CBAM (Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism) in Europe, and widening price gaps between domestic and international steel prices
- API pipe volumes remained subdued, declining sharply year-on-year due to a slowdown in tender activity; steel price volatility, safeguard duty implementation and slower execution of certain government-led projects weighed on the year
- Manufacturing capability breadth — the Company states it is the only player in India able to manufacture MS pipes from 0.6 mm to 25 mm thickness and pipe sizes from half an inch to 140 inches, on a manufacturing capacity of 14.21 lakh tonnes per annum
- Registration in Neom city, a new urban area planned by Saudi Arabia, is expected to enable supply of pipes to new city projects, with active enquiries already received
- Steel business order book exceeding Rs 1,000 crore at year-end, led primarily by exports, spiral pipes and domestic API orders, providing strong visibility going into 2026-27
- Professional Lighting concluded the year with an order book of Rs 160 crore, providing healthy near-term visibility
- Order from Oil and Natural Gas Corporation secured after successfully manufacturing API 5CT casing pipes using ERW technology for the first time in India

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: Pressure from new labor laws (₹30-40 Cr impact), rising fuel/power costs, and imported raw materials for Lighting (30-35% import content). Domestic API/tender margins compressed due to competition; offset by high-margin US exports.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Strict 1/3 rule: 1/3 to dividends (₹5.00/share declared for FY26), 1/3 to business growth/working capital, 1/3 to capex. Considering share buyback as regulations ease.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Surya Roshni continued brownfield capacity building across its steel pipe network during 2025-26. The Board's report states that capacity expansion initiatives across Anjar, Gwalior, Bahadurgarh and Hindupur, along with the addition of new DFT (Direct Forming Technology) lines, are aligned to support the growth trajectory in structural, API and value-added pipes; the Chairman similarly reports that capacity expansions continued across Bahadurgarh, Gwalior, Anjar and Hindupur, aimed at strengthening participation in structural pipes, API pipes, spiral pipes and value-added applications. Ramp-up at newer facilities, particularly spiral and Cold Rolled Strips (CRS) operations, is described as progressing in line with internal benchmarks and supporting incremental operating leverage, with capacity utilisation across plants remaining well balanced and production redirected internally towards higher-demand, value-accretive categories. During the year the segment achieved a first-in-India milestone by manufacturing API 5CT casing pipes using ERW technology, which enabled an order from Oil and Natural Gas Corporation. On the consumer side, entry into wires and cables was backed by an investment of Rs 25 crore, with the Turbo Flex range manufactured entirely in-house at the Malanpur facility. The AR's history line-up records the preceding build-out: the Hindupur steel pipe plant (2017, scaled to 1,50,000 MT), 3LPE coated pipe units at Anjar (2019 and 2021), a third galvanised plant at Hindupur taking total capacity to 2,00,000 MT (2021), a large-diameter DFT facility at Gwalior (2022), LED component manufacturing including drivers, PCBs, MCPCBs, housings and diffusers (2023), spiral pipe production at Gwalior and a new cold rolled plant at Bahadurgarh (2024-25), and in 2025-26 advanced backward integration through LED component manufacturing under the PLI scheme.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Cautiously optimistic but defensive on past misses; Emphasizes 'conservative guidance' to avoid over-promising; Confident on FY27 being a 'record year' driven by exports; Transparent about labor/fuel headwinds.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Established Surya brand with a diversified customer base and extensive distribution reach across domestic and export markets
- Multi-location manufacturing network across Bahadurgarh, Anjar, Hindupur and Malanpur for steel, and Kashipur and Malanpur for lighting
- Integrated platform for production, design and innovation through the Surya Technology & Innovation Centre (STIC) at Noida
- Value-added products contributed approximately 43% of total pipe volumes, shifting the mix towards higher-margin categories
- Totally debt free with a net cash surplus of Rs 337.00 crore as on 31st March, 2026, supporting a strong balance sheet
- Widened specification range at Bahadurgarh to pipes from 0.6 mm thickness onwards, addressing a wider set of applications
- Product breadth in exports of value-added products including hollow sections, coated pipes and specialised application pipes

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Geopolitical instability affecting exports; Delay in Indian government capex (Jal Jeevan/City Gas) impacting domestic volumes; Raw material (HR Coil) availability constraints; Execution risk on margin guidance given rising input costs.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Management explicitly lowered FY27 EBITDA/ton guidance (₹4,700) despite higher export mix, citing massive hidden cost inflation (labor/fuel) that peers may not be fully pricing in; The 'Middle East crisis' blocked 12k tons in Q4 but simultaneously accelerated the strategic pivot to the US market which offers double the EBITDA/ton.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Increase the share of value-added products in the steel mix — API, coated, spiral, hollow sections and specialised applications accounted for approximately 43% of total volumes, up from a business that was significantly more dependent on commodity products five years ago
- Grow exports from a volume-led to a higher-value driver: strengthen Europe, enter the UK market for section pipes and expand engagement across North America
- Continue brownfield capacity expansion in Steel — additional spiral pipe capacities, DFT-enabled offerings and cold rolling enhancements across Anjar, Gwalior, …

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Government scheme — PLI] Commenced a manufacturing facility for LED components under the PLI scheme, "Large Investment" category; incentive quantum is "4% to 6% on sales over the base year for a period of five years subsequent to the base year", with the "claim of 3rd year received and also eligible for 4th year claim".
- [Brand] "onboarding of cricketer Suryakumar Yadav as the brand ambassador for its Steel Tubes & Pipes business".
- [Governance] Board includes Executive Chairman Shri J. P. Agarwal (Padma Shri awardee) and two Managing Directors — Shri Raju Bista (past President of ELCOMA, presently a Member of Parliament) and Shri Vinay Surya.
- [Demand policy hooks] Steel demand case rests on government programmes — "Government thrust on high investments, CGD, Smart Cities, Nal se Jal" with "₹ 5 lac crore investment expected in 5 years"; PVC pipes cite "Housing for All, 'Nal se Jal', Project AMRUT and Swachh Bharat Mission" and a sector "expected to see an average Annual growth of 10%".
- [Recognition] Named among "Top 500 Value Creators 2025"; Ms. Puja Surya recognised as an Industry Leader by Economic Times for "Excellence in Integrated Manufacturing and Supply Chain".
